name: Equatorial Guinea
tagline: A volcanic island, and turtles on the black sand
summary: Bioko is a volcanic island with cloud forest, seven primate species and four nesting turtle species on its southern beaches; the mainland at Monte Alen holds gorillas and forest elephant.
when: The dry seasons. Turtle nesting on Bioko's south runs November to February.

entries.caption: Bioko
entries.description: A volcanic island in the Gulf of Guinea, forested to the summit and ringed by black sand.
entries.subject: the forested volcanic cone of Bioko rising above the sea

entries.caption: The Gran Caldera
entries.description: A collapsed volcanic crater in the south of Bioko, forested, and reached only on foot.
entries.subject: the forested rim of the Gran Caldera de Luba on Bioko

entries.caption: Seven Primates on One Island
entries.description: Bioko has seven species, several of them found on that island and nowhere else.
entries.subject: a Bioko drill monkey in the island's cloud forest

entries.caption: Monte Alen
entries.description: Mainland forest with gorilla, chimpanzee and forest elephant, walked rather than driven.
entries.subject: rainforest and a river valley in Monte Alen National Park

entries.caption: Pico Basile
entries.description: 3,011 metres, the island's volcano, with a road most of the way up it.
entries.subject: the summit and cloud forest of Pico Basile on Bioko

entries.caption: Iladyi
entries.description: A 250-metre cascade off the caldera rim in the south of Bioko.
entries.subject: the Iladyi cascade falling from the caldera rim on Bioko

entries.caption: The Wele and the Muni
entries.description: The Wele runs across the mainland; the Muni estuary marks the Gabonese border.
entries.subject: the Muni estuary with mangrove at low tide

entries.caption: Black Sand and Turtles
entries.description: Four species nest on Bioko's southern beaches — leatherback, green, olive ridley and hawksbill.
entries.subject: a leatherback turtle on black sand at Bioko's southern beach

entries.caption: Cloud Forest and Lowland
entries.description: Cloud forest above a thousand metres on Bioko, and Congo Basin forest on the mainland.
entries.subject: moss-covered cloud forest on the slopes of Pico Basile

entries.caption: Trekking the Caldera
entries.description: Three days on foot from Ureca to the Gran Caldera, through forest, with no road at all.
entries.subject: walkers on a forest trail towards the Gran Caldera

entries.caption: Spanish, Fang and Bubi
entries.description: The only Spanish-speaking country in Africa, with Fang on the mainland and Bubi on Bioko.
entries.subject: a street of Spanish colonial buildings in Malabo

entries.caption: The Bubi
entries.description: Bioko's first people, with their own language, and a history separate from the mainland.
entries.subject: a Bubi village on a forested slope on Bioko

entries.caption: Pepe Soup and Malamba
entries.description: Pepper soup with fish, and malamba — palm wine sweetened with cane.
entries.subject: a bowl of fish pepper soup with plantain

entries.caption: The Abira
entries.description: A Bubi purification ceremony, danced with drums and rattles.
entries.subject: Bubi dancers with rattles at a village ceremony on Bioko

entries.caption: Carving and Basketry
entries.description: Fang carving on the mainland, and Bubi basketry and wooden bells on Bioko.
entries.subject: a carved wooden Fang figure and woven basket

entries.caption: Colonial Malabo
entries.description: Santa Isabel was a Spanish port town, and the cathedral and customs house still stand.
entries.subject: the twin-spired Spanish colonial cathedral in Malabo

entries.caption: Nothing Listed Yet
entries.description: No World Heritage sites, and a colonial architecture that has been very little studied.
entries.subject: a decaying Spanish colonial verandah building in Malabo

entries.caption: Malabo and Bata
entries.description: The island capital in a drowned crater, and the mainland's largest city on the coast.
entries.subject: the harbour and colonial waterfront of Malabo

entries.caption: Spanish Colonial
entries.description: Malabo's cathedral, customs house and shuttered merchant houses, in a Gulf of Guinea version of Spain.
entries.subject: shuttered Spanish colonial houses on a Malabo street

entries.caption: Sunday After Mass
entries.description: Malabo empties into the streets after the cathedral, and stays there.
entries.subject: people gathered outside the cathedral in Malabo after mass

entries.caption: Beach and Forest
entries.description: Arena Blanca on Bioko is calm and shaded, and Pico Basile is drivable.
entries.subject: a family on the sheltered sand at Arena Blanca on Bioko

entries.caption: Walking Bioko
entries.description: The south of the island has no roads. Everything there is done on foot.
entries.subject: a forest path descending towards the sea on southern Bioko

entries.caption: Business Hotels, Mostly
entries.description: Malabo and Bata have good hotels built for the oil industry, and Bioko's south has none.
entries.subject: a hotel terrace overlooking the sea at Malabo

entries.caption: The Bioko Biodiversity Programme
entries.description: University-run monitoring of the turtle beaches and primates since 1998.
entries.subject: researchers recording a turtle nest on Bioko's black sand

entries.caption: Black Sand and Green
entries.description: Ureca in the rain, which is most of the time — the wettest place in Africa.
entries.subject: rain over black sand and rainforest at Ureca on Bioko

entries.caption: Annobon
entries.description: A volcanic island six hundred kilometres out, with a crater lake and four flights a month.
entries.subject: the crater lake and volcanic slopes of Annobon island

entries.caption: Why Equatorial Guinea
entries.description: Four turtle species on one black beach, under a forest with drills in it.
entries.subject: turtle tracks on black sand below rainforest at dawn
